answer: Use seed-rooted trust propagation over the interaction graph: a few verified honest agents act as seeds, and standing flows outward along real interaction edges, climbing toward a summit only agents with genuine ties to the honest region can reach. A sybil farm sits on a lonely knoll: its puppets mostly link to each other, so almost no trust reaches them, and buying real edges costs time and money. Limits: the seeds must stay honest, sparse graphs blur the boundary, and a patient attacker can slowly carve karst-like tunnels of trust into the honest region.
